facts.statement: The genus Koutalisaurus, meaning "spoon lizard" due to the shape of its jaw, is known from a mostly complete dentary found in the Late Cretaceous Tremp Formation near Abella de la Conca, Spain.
facts.quote: Koutalisaurus (meaning "spoon lizard", in reference to the shape of the dentary) is a potentially dubious genus of lambeosaurine hadrosaurid dinosaur based on a mostly complete dentary recovered from the Maastrichtian-aged (Late Cretaceous) Tremp Formation near the town of Abella de la Conca, Lleida, Spain.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, IPS SRA 27, was originally assigned to Pararhabdodon in 1999 before being reclassified as the new species Koutalisaurus kohlerorum by Prieto-Marquez et al. in 2006.
facts.quote: The holotype dentary, IPS SRA 27, had previously been referred to Pararhabdodon in 1999, but comes from a different locality, is based on non-comparable material, and has unusual characteristics, leading Prieto-Marquez et al. (2006) to place the dentary in the new species Koutalisaurus kohleorum.

facts.statement: Koutalisaurus was later considered an invalid nomen dubium, though subsequent studies continue to treat it as a valid genus.
facts.quote: Koutalisaurus was later found to be an invalid nomen dubium, although later studies do not reflect this hypothesis and still classify Koutalisaurus as a valid genus.

facts.statement: The dentary is very elongate with a long, toothless front portion bent steeply downward and inward, creating a spoon-like shape when complete.
facts.quote: The dentary is very elongate, and has a long toothless portion (the front of the jaw, including the end where the predentary would have been attached) that is bent steeply downward and inward, which would have given the jaw a spoon-like shape when complete.

facts.statement: The dentary is comparable in size to other hadrosaurids but is on the small side and possesses unusual proportions.
facts.quote: It is comparable in size, although on the small side and with unusual proportions (see above), compared to dentaries from other hadrosaurids.

facts.statement: Prieto-Marquez et al. (2006) classified the animal as a hadrosaurid but noted its uncertain placement within the family.
facts.quote: Prieto-Marquez et al. (2006) found the animal to be a hadrosaurid, but of uncertain placement within the family.

facts.statement: Recent work by Prieto-Marquez and Wagner suggests that Koutalisaurus is the same genus as Pararhabdodon, as originally hypothesized.
facts.quote: More recent work by Prieto-Marquez and Wagner suggests that it is the same as Pararhabdodon as originally thought.

facts.statement: A 2020 study by Nick Longrich and colleagues classified Koutalisaurus as an arenysaurin.
facts.quote: A 2020 study by Nick Longrich and colleagues describing the genus Ajnabia found Koutalisaurus to be an arenysaurin.

facts.statement: Koutalisaurus kohlerorum lived during the Late Cretaceous Maastrichtian, approximately 70 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: Koutalisaurus kohlerorum es la única especie conocida del género extinto Koutalisaurus ("lagarto cuchara") de dinosaurio ornitópodo hadrosáurido, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico en el Maastrichtiense, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Koutalisaurus is classified within the subfamily Lambeosaurinae.
Koutalisaurus belongs to the tribe Tsintaosaurini.
The genus Koutalisaurus was named by Prieto-Marquez, Gaete, Rivas, Galobart, and Boada in 2006.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Prieto-Marquez, Gaete, Rivas, Galobart, y Boada, 2006

facts.statement: The species Koutalisaurus kohlerorum was named by Prieto-Marquez et al. in 2006.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Koutalisaurus as Arenysaurini.
